intro: Mind your head. You are entering Kaymaklı Underground City, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province dating from the 1st millennium BC and extended under Byzantium. It is wider and lower-ceilinged than Derinkuyu, with four levels open to visitors, and its tunnels still run beneath the village houses above.
history: Kaymaklı is broader and lower than Derinkuyu, and its corridors are narrow enough that you have to stoop. Notice how the rooms cluster around courtyards. Each cluster is laid out like a separate household, with its own kitchen and stores. And life still goes on above you: the village stands on these tunnels, and some of them are still used for storage.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the stables and the church, then the stores and kitchens. Look for the basalt workshop stone, and glance up at the ventilation shafts.
facts: Did you know? A nine-kilometre tunnel is said to link Kaymaklı to Derinkuyu. The claim is unproven, but the galleries between the two have never been fully mapped. The corridors were made low and narrow on purpose: an attacker who got in had to stoop, and go single file. And the village above still stands on these tunnels, its people still using parts of them for storage.
outro: This brings our journey through Kaymaklı Underground City to an end. Before you climb back into the daylight, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these tunnels keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
